provider: NASA JPL Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS)
dataset: Fireball and bolide reports (SSD/CNEOS Fireball Data API)
description: Bright meteors (fireballs / bolides) detected by U.S. Government sensors: time and location of peak brightness, radiated energy, estimated impact energy, altitude and velocity.

coverage.temporal: The five years before the current date (the archive itself starts in 1988)

updateCadence.upstream: Irregular – events are added days to weeks after they occur

attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech, Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) fireball data

license.name: NASA/JPL data – generally not copyrighted; JPL asks for credit
license.notes: The API documentation asks users to avoid concurrent requests and to check the signature/version of each response. Credit NASA/JPL-Caltech (CNEOS).

limitations: Not a complete record: only events reported by U.S. Government sensors are included, and reporting is delayed by days to weeks.
Location is the point of peak brightness, reported to 0.1 degree; many events have no reported location and are omitted (req-loc=true).
Impact energy is an estimate derived by CNEOS from the radiated energy with an empirical relation.
confidenceNotes: CNEOS publishes no per-event confidence, so none is shown. Severity is derived by this application from the estimated impact energy (kilotons of TNT).

retention.note: Events are kept for ten years after they occurred.

layers.name: Fireballs (bolides)
layers.description: Bright meteors reported by U.S. Government sensors, at the location of peak brightness.
